extracted.intended_audience: researchers, prospective grant applicants, research administrators, and historians of scientific funding (primarily chemistry/physics)
extracted.subtask_description: A listing of awarded scientific research project support: principal investigators, project titles, institutional affiliation, project codes, award durations (months), and dollar amounts, organized by discipline and U.S. state/institution. Serves as a historical/administrative record of funded projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal investigator (PI) name
rubrics_metrics.description: The investigator(s) listed for each award (formatted as last name, initials or last name, first name). Example entries: 'DEHMELT, HANS U', 'WILLIAMS, ROBERT W'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PI names are presented alongside project titles and institutions; multiple PIs may be grouped on one line (e.g., 'WILLIAMS, ROBERT W, AND COOK, VICTOR').

rubrics_metrics.name: Project title
rubrics_metrics.description: The research project title or short project descriptor appearing after the PI name. Examples: 'ISOLATED ATOMIC PARTICLES FLOATING AT REST IN FREE SPACE', 'PHOTOLYSIS OF CHLOROPROPENES, AND REACTIONS OF HYDROXYL RADICALS'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles vary in length; they are the primary description of the funded work and often use technical field terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project code / identifier
rubrics_metrics.description: Parenthetical codes following project titles (e.g., '(POiUt OOi)', '(P0J06H)i', '(PC3li666)'). These appear to be internal project or program identifiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codes often include letters/numbers and appear in parentheses immediately after the title; formatting varies and sometimes includes spacing, punctuation, or capitalization inconsistencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award duration (months)
rubrics_metrics.description: The funded project duration expressed in months (e.g., '12 MONTHS', '24 MONTHS', '84 MONTHS', '6 MONTHS').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duration is given as a whole number of months and is listed immediately before or after the award amount; can indicate short-term or multi-year support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount (dollars)
rubrics_metrics.description: The dollar value of the award for the listed duration, shown with a dollar sign and comma grouping (e.g., '$46,800', '$424,900', '$6,700').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amounts appear adjacent to durations and are given in U.S. dollars; formatting in the source text sometimes contains OCR/artifact errors but the intended numeric amount is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution / organizational affiliation
rubrics_metrics.description: The university, college, or research organization associated with the PI (e.g., 'UNIVERSITY OF WISCONSIN, MADISON', 'STANFORD UNIVERSITY', 'CALIFORNIA STATE UNIVERSITY, LONG BEACH').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions are used to group and present awards and are often preceded by state headings; may include campus/location and occasionally program labels (e.g., 'BLACK COLLEGES (FOUR-YEAR)').

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline/category heading
rubrics_metrics.description: Top-level headings that categorize listings by field or discipline (example: 'CHEMISTRY').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listings are organized under discipline headings, which provide context for the subject matter of the projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic / state grouping
rubrics_metrics.description: State-level headings used to group institutions and awards (e.g., 'UTAH', 'VIRGINIA', 'CALIFORNIA', 'COLORADO').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State headings precede institutional listings; organizational structure of the document groups awards by state then by institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program / funding category label
rubrics_metrics.description: Programmatic labels that identify the type of support, for example 'SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH PROJECT SUPPORT' appears as a section header.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section headers indicate the program or funding mechanism under which awards were made and can include subprograms or special initiatives (e.g., conferences, task orders, undergraduate participation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special program or award subtype annotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotations describing special award types or program subcategories found in some entries, such as 'UNDERGRADUATE RESEARCH PARTICIPATION', 'BLACK COLLEGES (FOUR-YEAR)', 'TASK ORDER FOR A STUDY'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These phrases identify targeted or special-purpose grants and are sometimes appended to the project or institution lines; they signal award intent or beneficiary population.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple/cooperative investigators or collaborative projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries that list more than one investigator or cross-institution collaborations (e.g., 'SHELDON, WILLIAM R; COSMIC RAY STUDIES', 'SHULER, KURT L, MAYER, JOSEPH E, WEARE, JOHN K, AND WHEELER, JOHN C; THEORETICAL CHEMISTRY').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaboration is indicated by multiple names separated by commas or 'AND'; may imply joint projects or shared support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting/metadata artifacts (project listing conventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conventions in the listing such as uppercase titles, parentheses for codes, placement of months and amounts, and occasional OCR/text artifacts (e.g., inconsistent spacing, capitalization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not evaluation criteria, these conventions define how information is presented and should be considered when parsing or extracting structured data from the document.
